main_cup.name: Algerian Cup (Coupe d'Algerie / Coupe de la Republique)
main_cup.participants: open to all clubs of the Algerian league system; 64 clubs from the first national round (2026-27 infobox: '64 (as of first national round)')
main_cup.winner_berth: CAF Confederation Cup (plus Algerian Super Cup)
main_cup.quote: dates = 4 December 2026 - 1 May 2027 ... The winners automatically qualify for both the CAF Confederation Cup and the Algerian Super Cup the following year.
main_cup.note: Final is a single match at a national stadium (Nelson Mandela Stadium, Algiers in 2025 and 2026); no two-legged final in the current format.

countries.super_cup: Algerian Super Cup (cup winner vs league champion)

main_cup.name: Ethiopian Cup
main_cup.participants: clubs of the Ethiopian league system; entry count not documented in the sources checked
main_cup.winner_berth: CAF Confederation Cup (assumed; not stated in the source)
main_cup.quote: The Ethiopian Cup is the top knockout tournament of the Ethiopian football. It was created in 1945. ... 2025/26 Welwalo Adigrat University 2-0 Sidama Bunna
main_cup.note: No season articles exist on Wikipedia, and no round dates are published; only the final result is recorded (RSSSF page last updated 26 Jul 2026, so the 2025-26 final was played before late July). Format/berth inferred from the standard Ethiopian pattern, not sourced.

main_cup.name: Ghana FA Cup (MTN FA Cup)
main_cup.participants: 110 clubs: 92 in the preliminary round, 64 in the main competition including 32 qualifiers; Premier League clubs enter the main draw
main_cup.quote: dates = 24 October 2025 - 31 May 2026 ... num_teams = 110 ... 92 (preliminary round) ... 64 (main competition incl. 32 qualifiers)
main_cup.note: Berth not printed in the season article; taken from the standard Ghanaian cup-winner slot.

main_cup.name: Libyan Cup (Al-Fatih Cup)
main_cup.participants: Libyan clubs of the top divisions; field is small and the recent editions are compressed, no entry count published
main_cup.winner_berth: CAF Confederation Cup (assumed; not stated in the source)
main_cup.note: 2023-24 edition was not played; the 2025 and 2026 finals were staged abroad in Cairo. No round dates published anywhere checked, so the window is left null.

main_cup.name: Throne Cup (Coupe du Trone)
main_cup.participants: clubs from all tiers through 4 preliminary rounds; final phase is a 32-team round of 32 made of the 16 Botola clubs plus 16 qualifiers (64 teams from the third round onwards)
main_cup.winner_berth: CAF Confederation Cup (reallocated to the runner-up if the winner is already in the Champions League)
main_cup.quote: The current format features 4 preliminary rounds and the final phase. All games are one-legged. ... The winners of the Throne Cup qualify for the following season's CAF Confederation Cup.
main_cup.note: Window is irregular: the 2023-24 edition played its quarter-finals on 14-15 June 2025, so a fixed annual window cannot be stated. Some rounds were two-legged in earlier periods; the current format is one-legged with a single final, usually at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat.

main_cup.name: Nigeria Federation Cup (President Federation Cup)
main_cup.participants: 74 clubs (70 in 2026) - the winners and runners-up of each of the 36 state cups plus the FCT; a rookie play-off among the 20 lowest-ranked clubs sends 10 into the 54-team first round
main_cup.winner_berth: CAF Confederation Cup (plus Nigeria Super Cup)
main_cup.quote: dates = 6 May - 11 July 2026 ... The tournament began with the National playoffs on 6 May.
main_cup.note: All matches are played at neutral venues; replays existed historically (1968, 1972 finals) but not in the current format.

main_cup.name: Coupe du Senegal
main_cup.participants: 64 teams in the final phase (32es de finale), professionals, semi-pros and amateurs, single pot from the round of 32
main_cup.quote: participants = 64 equipes (phase finale) ... Le tirage au sort a ete effectue le 16 janvier 2026 ... Le vainqueur de la competition se qualifie pour le tour de qualification de la Coupe de la confederation 2026-2027.
main_cup.note: Penalties decide drawn matches from the round of 32; extra time only from the semi-finals. The draw was on 16 January 2026 but the source gives no round dates, so no window is stated.

main_cup.name: Nedbank Cup
main_cup.participants: 32-club main draw: 16 Premiership clubs (automatic), 8 National First Division clubs (via qualifiers) and 8 amateur clubs
main_cup.quote: dates = 4 February 2026 - ... Final: date = 2 May 2026 ... Durban City 2-1 TS Galaxy, Peter Mokaba Stadium, Polokwane.
main_cup.note: No replays: drawn matches go to extra time and penalties. Final is a single match at a neutral venue.

countries.second_cup: Carling Knockout (already documented in league-cups.json); MTN 8 is the separate top-8 league cup

main_cup.name: Tunisian Cup (Coupe de Tunisie)
main_cup.participants: clubs of Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 plus lower-tier qualifiers; 8 Ligue 1 clubs enter in the round of 32 and the other 6 in the next round
main_cup.winner_berth: CAF Confederation Cup (finalist takes the slot if the winner is already in the Champions League)
main_cup.quote: dates = 3 April - 1 June 2025 ... The Tunisian Cup champion qualifies directly for the CAF Confederation Cup.
main_cup.note: Window is from the last completed edition (2024-25); the 2025-26 edition ran into 2026 with the round-of-16 draw on 27 February 2026. Final is a single match; two-legged finals appear only in older editions.

main_cup.name: Uganda Cup
main_cup.participants: 168 clubs, the largest field in the region, drawn from the top flight down to regional/amateur clubs
main_cup.quote: number of teams = 168 ... The winner of the competition represents Uganda in the CAF Confederations Cup ... the current holders are BUL FC who won the cup by defeating VIPERS SC 3-1 on 12 June 2022 in Masindi district.
main_cup.note: No season articles exist for recent editions and no round calendar is published; only the fact that recent finals were played in June (12 June 2022, Masindi) is documented. Format assumed single-leg knockout.

countries.second_cup: Uganda Super 8 (top-8 league cup, not a national cup)
